hyps.why: If edge 0 is none, node 1 is identically zero, so a conv on edge 1->3 has no input to process and the edit is nearly useless.
With edge 0 none, node 1 carries no signal, so adding a conv on edge 1->2 contributes nothing.
When edge 2->3 is cut, the direct input->output edge becomes one of the few paths to the output, so giving it a strong conv matters more.
Cutting edge 2->3 when edge 0->3 is already none removes most or all routes to the output, risking a near-disconnected cell.
If node 1 is dead, node 2 can only be fed via edge 0->2, so a conv there is the main route for computation through node 2.
Removing an existing 3x3 conv on the direct edge loses far more capacity than removing a pool or skip.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with parameter-free pooling on the first edge strips the main feature extractor feeding nodes 1, 2 and 3.
Turning a missing edge into a conv adds a whole new computational path, a bigger gain than upgrading an existing op.
If edge 0->2 is already none, cutting edge 1->2 leaves node 2 empty and makes edge 2->3 useless.
Adding a residual input->output connection where none existed helps optimization much more than swapping out an existing op for skip.
